sections.overview: Paradarisa consonaria, the Square Spot, is a geometrid moth recorded in parts of western Europe. Older sources may use the combination Ectropis consonaria.
sections.identification: The adult wingspan is about 40–45 mm. A dark square mark on the forewing is useful for identification, although the species is variable and dark melanistic forms occur.
sections.habitat: It is associated with woodland. French records place it mainly in northern and central France.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on trees, including oak and birch.
sections.behavior: In Britain adults fly mainly from April to June.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillars develop on woody food plants before pupating. The sources consulted document eggs and larvae but do not establish a species-wide development schedule.
sections.ecology: Because wing colour varies, the square forewing mark is more dependable than overall darkness alone. The larvae use several kinds of trees rather than one narrowly specialized host.
sections.conservation: The consulted sources describe regional records but do not establish a global conservation assessment or population trend for this moth.
